knowledge-base.name: e2e-testing
knowledge-base.triggers: end-to-end test, e2e, UI test, browser test, integration test, acceptance test, smoke test, regression, playwright test, /end-to-end-test
knowledge-base.overview: E2E UI testing via browser automation. Tests verify what the USER sees, not what the developer expects. Every test requires browser-based evidence. No database shortcuts. No fabricated results.

e2e-philosophy.principle: E2E tests verify the user's experience, not the developer's intent
A test that passes via a database shortcut proves nothing about what the user sees
Every test case must be reproducible by a human sitting at a browser
Evidence is not optional — it is the output of the test
An honest FAIL is more valuable than a fabricated PASS
The database can be written to by background jobs and migrations. Finding a record in the database does not prove the UI created it.

knowledge-base.filter-testing-note:
Unit tests for filter transformation logic (LINQ-to-Objects) do not catch SQL-level bugs. EF Core null compensation only activates in real SQL: a NOT LIKE on a null column silently adds OR IS NULL, so a DoesNotContain filter will include rows with null values unless an explicit IsNotNullOrEmpty guard is present. Unit tests pass regardless because LINQ-to-Objects handles nulls differently than SQL Server.
Always run a browser test against real data when any of these apply: - A new field is added to a filter that can hold null values - A DoesNotContain / None of filter is added or modified - A Blank / IsNullOrEmpty or IsNotNullOrEmpty filter is added or modified - A field's projection changes (e.g., int? to string)
The acceptance test: set the filter in a browser, check the member count is reasonable. Blank should return only members with no value. None of should exclude the selected values AND members with no recorded value.
Root cause from ASC-1201: null was projected as null instead of "", so IsNullOrEmpty("") had nothing to match (Blank returned 0). The DoesNotContain guard was missing, so members with null values were included in None of results. Both bugs passed unit tests and code review because the SQL behavior was never tested in a browser.

anti-cheat-patterns.description: Catalog of testing shortcuts that produce false results. Recognize these patterns and refuse them.

cheat.name: Database Shortcut
cheat.description: Querying the database directly to verify that a UI action persisted data, instead of observing the result in the UI.
cheat.example-bad: Run: sqlite3 app.db "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email='test@test.com'" to verify signup worked.
cheat.example-good: After signup, navigate to the user list or profile page and verify the user appears there using browser_snapshot.
cheat.why-banned: The database can be written to by background jobs, migrations, or direct DB access. Finding a record proves the database was written — NOT that the UI created it correctly. The user cannot query the database; they can only see the UI.

cheat.name: Fabricated Pass
cheat.description: Marking a test PASS without executing any browser actions to verify it, or based solely on code reading.
cheat.example-bad: Marking TC-005 PASS because the code reads `if (success) { setMessage("Saved!") }` — so it "should" work.
cheat.example-good: Click Save, call browser_snapshot to confirm the success message appears in the accessibility tree, then take a screenshot with the message annotated.
cheat.why-banned: Code can be correct but produce wrong UI due to conditional rendering, CSS visibility, async timing bugs, or race conditions. Only the browser shows what the user actually sees.

cheat.name: Irrelevant Screenshot
cheat.description: Taking a screenshot of a page or state unrelated to the test case and presenting it as evidence.
cheat.example-bad: Screenshotting the home page as evidence that the "Create Product" form saved correctly.
cheat.example-good: After submitting the Create Product form, navigate to the product list, call browser_snapshot to confirm the new item appears in text, then screenshot the list with a red annotation box around the new item.
cheat.why-banned: Evidence must directly demonstrate the assertion. A home page screenshot proves the home page loads — nothing else.

cheat.name: Pre-Action Screenshot
cheat.description: Taking the screenshot before performing the test steps, then using it as the AFTER screenshot.
cheat.example-bad: Take screenshot, then click Delete, then mark PASS using the pre-delete screenshot as "evidence."
cheat.example-good: Click Delete, wait for the item to disappear, call browser_snapshot to confirm absence in text, then screenshot the updated list.
cheat.why-banned: The AFTER screenshot must show the post-action state. A pre-action screenshot proves nothing about what the action did.

cheat.name: API Bypass
cheat.description: Using browser_evaluate to call the app's internal API endpoints directly, bypassing the UI form flow.
cheat.example-bad: browser_evaluate: fetch('/api/users', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({email: 'test@test.com'}) }) to "create a user" without using the UI form.
cheat.example-good: Navigate to /register, fill the form fields using browser_fill_form, click Submit, verify the success state via browser_snapshot.
cheat.why-banned: Calling the API directly tests the API, not the UI. Bugs in form validation, client-side logic, error messages, and UI feedback are completely invisible when bypassing the form.

cheat.name: Selective Test Execution
cheat.description: Running only the easy tests and omitting hard ones from the report without marking them BLOCKED.
cheat.example-bad: Omitting TC-012 (error state for invalid input) from the report because triggering a validation error requires specific setup.
cheat.example-good: Attempt TC-012 — submit the form with invalid input, call browser_snapshot to check whether validation messages appear, mark PASS or FAIL based on actual observation.
cheat.why-banned: Skipped tests hide bugs. The test plan is a contract — all items must be resolved.

scope-boundary.description: E2E tests cover full user journeys that span UI interaction, network calls, and observable server-side effects. Anything that doesn't cross that boundary belongs in unit or integration tests — not here.

belongs-in-e2e.item: Full journey: user fills a form → submits → server persists data → user sees confirmation or updated state
Authentication flow: unauthenticated user hits protected route → redirected to login → authenticates → lands on original destination
State visible after server round-trip: create an entity → reload the page → entity is still shown (proves the server persisted it, not just client state)
Cross-page flow: action on page A produces a visible effect on page B (e.g., add to cart on /products → count badge updates on /cart)
Error state from the server: submit a form that triggers a server-side validation error → verify the error message appears in the UI
Role-based visibility: log in as a non-admin → verify admin-only UI elements are absent

does-not-belong-in-e2e.item: Client-only field validation: a required-field message shown by the browser before any server call — this is a unit test for the validator function
Computed display values: a price total calculated from quantities already on the page — unit test the calculation function
Pure API response shape: whether an endpoint returns the right JSON — this is an integration/contract test
CSS or styling assertions: whether a button is red or a font is bold — these break on design changes and test nothing functional
Framework behavior: whether React re-renders when state changes, whether a router redirects on push — test the app, not the framework
Internal component state: whether a dropdown is "open" in React state — test the visible UI result (options appear), not the internal representation

scope-boundary.drift-detection:
If a TC could be fully verified by calling a function directly — no browser, no server round-trip, no multi-page navigation — it belongs in unit tests. Drop it from the E2E plan or move it to a "## Unit Coverage Notes" section in plan-draft.md.
Warning signs that a TC has drifted into unit-test territory: - The TC tests only one UI element in isolation (no user goal, no journey) - The TC verifies a value computed entirely in the browser (no server involved) - The TC checks whether something is styled correctly rather than whether it works - The TC could be automated without opening a browser at all
scope-boundary.test-pyramid-position:
E2E tests sit at the top of the pyramid: few in number, high in value, slow to run. For a typical app: - 70%+ of tests should be unit tests (fast, isolated, cheap) - 20% integration tests (API contracts, DB writes, service boundaries) - 10% E2E tests (critical user journeys only)
If a test plan has more than 40 TCs for a modest CRUD app, it likely contains unit-level tests that shouldn't be there. Review for drift before finalizing.

intelligent-test-generation.description: Rules for generating appropriate test coverage without combinatorial explosion. Apply these during test plan generation.

rule.name: Enum Exhaustion
rule.applies-to: toggle, select, radio group, segmented control
rule.condition: Control has N discrete states and N is 7 or fewer
rule.action: Generate ONE test case per state. A 3-option toggle (yes/no/undefined) → 3 TCs.
rule.rationale: Small enums are cheap to exhaust. Each state is a distinct code path. Skipping any state leaves bugs uncaught.

rule.name: Large Enum Boundary Values
rule.condition: Control has N discrete states and N is more than 7
rule.action: Generate 3 TCs: first option, last option, one invalid/out-of-range option.
rule.rationale: Exhausting 50 dropdown options is pointless churn. First/last/invalid catches the boundary bugs that matter.

rule.name: Boolean Controls
rule.action: Always generate exactly 2 TCs: enabled state and disabled state.

rule.name: List and Collection Coverage
rule.applies-to: lists, tables, grids, feeds, todo lists, grocery lists
rule.action: Always generate exactly these 4 TCs — no more, no fewer:
rule.tc: Empty state — list has zero items. Verify empty state message renders.
One item — list has exactly one item. Verify it renders correctly.
Several items — list has 3 to 5 items. Verify layout handles multiple items.
Full or maximum — list has many items or hits a page boundary. Verify pagination or scroll works.
rule.forbidden: Do NOT test every permutation of item content. The content of items does not matter — the COUNT does.
rule.rationale: Empty state catches missing placeholder UI. One item catches singular/plural bugs. Several items catches layout issues. Full catches pagination. These 4 cases cover the real failure modes.

rule.name: Form Validation
rule.action: Generate ONE TC per validation rule, not one TC per field.

validation-tc-types.type: Required field blank — submit with empty required field, verify error message
Invalid format — submit email field with non-email value, verify format error
Max length — submit field at limit and over limit, verify behavior
Cross-field validation — if fields have dependencies (e.g., password confirmation), test the mismatch case

rule.forbidden: Do NOT generate one TC per field × one TC per rule. That is a combinatorial explosion with no additional coverage value.

rule.name: UI Consistency
rule.applies-to: any component type with multiple instances across pages
rule.action: Generate ONE UI consistency TC per component type that has multiple instances.
rule.what-to-check: Same HTML element type, same aria role, same interaction model (click vs keyboard).
rule.rationale: A dropdown implemented with <select> in one place and a custom div in another is a bug waiting to happen — accessibility, keyboard nav, and automation all break differently.

always-include.tc: TC-SMOKE-01: Home page loads without console errors
TC-SMOKE-02: All primary nav links resolve without 404 or error page

intelligent-test-generation.pre-generation-requirement:
Build flow-map.md BEFORE writing any test cases. This is a hard gate — do not write a single TC until the flow map exists at workspace/[task-id]/flow-map.md.
The flow map must: 1. List every user journey (a goal a real user wants to accomplish, spanning multiple pages) 2. Score each journey by risk: auth/authz (+3), write operations (+2), primary conversion path (+3), multi-page flow (+1), external integration (+2), known prior bug (+3) 3. Include all journeys scoring 3 or higher, plus smoke tests 4. Document the most direct entry path to each journey (no roundabout navigation)
Every TC must reference its parent journey: TC-NNN [Journey: J# — Name, Step N] — description. Smoke tests use: TC-NNN [Journey: smoke] — description.

token-efficiency-protocol.description: Minimize token consumption without sacrificing evidence quality. Screenshots are expensive; use text-based verification first.

principle.name: Snapshot-First
principle.rule: Confirm the expected state exists in the accessibility tree text before capturing an image
principle.why: browser_snapshot returns text (cheap). browser_take_screenshot returns an image (expensive). Verify in text first, image only as final evidence.

principle.name: Screenshot on Pass Only
principle.rule: If browser_snapshot does NOT confirm the expected state, mark FAIL immediately
Record the observed snapshot text as the failure evidence — no screenshot needed
principle.why: A failed test needs a description of what went wrong, not an image of the wrong state. Saves significant token cost on failure cases.

principle.name: Discovery Phase Text Only
principle.rule: During app discovery (Phase 1), use browser_snapshot for all page crawling
Take only ONE browser_take_screenshot for the initial landing page
principle.why: Discovery is reconnaissance, not evidence collection. Text snapshots give all the information needed to build the component registry and App Map.

principle.name: Batch Annotations
principle.rule: When multiple elements on the same page need annotation, inject all overlays before taking ONE screenshot
Remove all overlays after the single screenshot
Example: for a UI consistency TC showing two inconsistent dropdowns on the same page, inject two overlays, take one screenshot, remove both
principle.why: Each browser_evaluate call costs tokens. Batching reduces the number of round-trips for multi-element annotation.

principle.name: Skip Before Screenshots for Smoke Tests
principle.rule: For smoke tests and navigation tests, skip the BEFORE screenshot
Include BEFORE screenshot only for state-change tests: create, update, delete, toggle
principle.why: A nav test BEFORE screenshot shows the same page as the AFTER screenshot in most cases. No additional evidence value.

principle.name: Navigation Batch Mode
principle.rule: For all navigation TCs (do all nav links resolve?), execute them in sequence: navigate, snapshot title/status, record in text, then screenshot each page once
Check for 404 in the snapshot text before committing to a screenshot
principle.why: Nav tests are rapid and cheap in text form. Group them together to avoid per-test overhead.

screenshot-annotation-technique.purpose: Mark the specific element or region being verified so screenshots are self-documenting evidence
screenshot-annotation-technique.requirement: Required for any test that verifies a specific button, form field, error message, list item, or UI element. Not required for full-page load tests.
screenshot-annotation-technique.remove-snippet: // Remove annotation overlay via browser_evaluate (call after screenshot) (function(){ const e = document.getElementById('__e2e_ann__'); if (e) e.remove(); })();

workflow.step: Call browser_snapshot — confirm expected state in text
Identify the visible text label of the element to annotate (button text, field label, list item)

Call browser_evaluate with text-find-snippet, substituting the label — if element has no unique text, use coordinate-inject-snippet instead. Both snippets return true on success, false if the element was not found or has zero dimensions.

ANNOTATION GATE — check the return value from browser_evaluate: - true → overlay present and visible. Proceed to screenshot. - false or null → element not found or off-screen. FAIL the TC with: "Annotation target '[label]' not found in DOM or has zero dimensions — element may not be rendered." Call remove-snippet to clean up. Do NOT call browser_take_screenshot. Skip to console check step.
Only if step 3b passed: call browser_take_screenshot — the red overlay is visible in the image. Save to PROOF_DIR.
Update plan.md with the screenshot filename

coordinate-guidance.source: browser_snapshot accessibility tree contains element bounding boxes. Use these for x/y/w/h values when falling back to coordinate-inject-snippet.
coordinate-guidance.fallback: If element has no unique text label, fall back to coordinate-inject-snippet with values from browser_snapshot.
coordinate-guidance.never: Never leave a test screenshot unannotated when a specific element is the point of verification.

visual-analysis-protocol.description: Claude analyzes every screenshot for visual problems before marking PASS. The accessibility tree confirms DOM structure. Vision confirms what the user actually sees. No external API. No separate tool. Claude's vision is already available on every screenshot.
visual-analysis-protocol.mandatory-questions: After every browser_take_screenshot, answer all of these before marking PASS: 1. Is any important element visually clipped by the viewport edge? 2. Is text overlapping other elements? 3. Are there broken images (alt text visible instead of rendered image)? 4. Does the layout look correct at this viewport? No unexpected overflow or stacking? 5. Is the element being verified actually visible — not behind a modal or off-screen? 6. For responsive tests: is there horizontal scroll where there shouldn't be?
visual-analysis-protocol.verdict: Any YES answer above = FAIL, even if DOM snapshot passed. Evidence: describe the visual problem in plain text. No extra screenshot needed for visual FAIL. Include in evidence table: TC-NNN | Visual: [description] | FAIL | (no screenshot)
visual-analysis-protocol.dom-pass-is-not-enough: The accessibility tree reports element presence and ARIA roles. It does not report: visual position, overlap, clipping, color, image load status. A button with correct ARIA that is visually hidden behind a modal = user cannot click it = FAIL. Always check both.

pixelmatch-baseline-protocol.description: Local pixel diff against saved baseline screenshots. Catches visual regressions that Claude's per-test vision misses because it has no memory of what the page looked like in a prior session. Pure npm, no external API, runs offline.
pixelmatch-baseline-protocol.setup: pixelmatch ships as an npm package. One-time install per project: npm install pixelmatch pngjs --save-dev
pixelmatch-baseline-protocol.first-run: When no baseline exists for the current page: 1. Save screenshot to workspace/[task-id]/baselines/[page-slug].png 2. Log: "Baseline saved for [page-slug]. Future runs will compare against this." 3. Do NOT mark FAIL — baseline is being established.
pixelmatch-baseline-protocol.threshold-guidance: 0.03 (3%) is the default. Fine-tune per project: - Apps with animations or live data: increase to 0.08 - Pixel-perfect design systems: decrease to 0.01 Store threshold in workspace/[task-id]/visual-config.json if customized.
pixelmatch-baseline-protocol.page-slug-convention: Derive from URL path: replace / with - and strip leading dash. / → home /products/list → products-list /settings → settings /admin/users/new → admin-users-new

ui-consistency-pass.description: Detect structural mismatches across instances of the same component type. One TC per component type with multiple instances.

what-to-check.check: HTML element type: does every dropdown use <select>, or do some use custom divs?
ARIA roles: does every dialog have role="dialog", or are some missing it?
Interaction model: do all buttons respond to keyboard Enter, or only some?
Class naming: does every card use the same CSS class pattern?

process.step: Navigate to the page containing the canonical (first) instance of the component type
Call browser_snapshot, extract the element type and aria role
Navigate to each subsequent page with another instance
Call browser_snapshot, compare element type and aria role
If all consistent: PASS — record in plan.md with a note ("all dropdowns use <select>")
If inconsistent: inject overlays on BOTH the canonical and deviant instances, take ONE screenshot, mark FAIL with description

ui-consistency-pass.example-fail: Dropdown on /products renders as <select id="sort">; dropdown on /orders renders as <div role="combobox"> — structural inconsistency across pages
ui-consistency-pass.example-pass: All 4 status toggles across the app use <input type="radio"> with role="radio" — consistent

category.name: Smoke Tests
category.tc: Home page loads without console errors (browser_console_messages must be empty of errors)
All primary nav links resolve without 404 — check status code and page content in browser_snapshot

category.name: Authentication Flows
category.tc: Login with valid credentials → verify user is authenticated (name/avatar visible, protected content accessible)
Login with invalid credentials → verify error message appears in UI (not just absence of redirect)
Logout → verify user is logged out (redirect to login page, protected routes block)
Navigate to protected route without auth → verify redirect to login page

category.name: CRUD Operations
category.tc: Create: Fill form, submit via UI, verify new entity appears in list/detail view — browser_snapshot must show the new item
Read list: Navigate to list view, verify entities render — browser_snapshot checks for expected items
Read detail: Navigate to detail view, verify all expected fields are present in browser_snapshot
Update: Open edit form, change a field, save via UI, verify change appears in list or detail view
Delete: Trigger delete action via UI, confirm dialog if present, verify entity removed from list in browser_snapshot
Empty state: Navigate to list with no data — verify empty state message renders (not blank page)

category.name: Navigation
category.tc: Each primary nav link resolves without 404 or error page
Browser back button returns to previous page correctly
Links within page content navigate correctly
Page title or breadcrumb matches current location

category.name: Error States
category.tc: Submit form with required field blank → verify validation message appears in UI
Submit email field with invalid format → verify format error appears
Navigate to a nonexistent path (e.g., /this-does-not-exist) → verify 404 page renders (not blank, not stack trace)

category.name: Responsive Behavior
category.tc: Mobile (375px width): Key pages render without horizontal scroll — use browser_resize to 375x667 before snapshot
Tablet (768px width): Layout adapts, content accessible — browser_resize to 768x1024
Desktop (1280px width): Full layout, no content clipping — browser_resize to 1280x900
category.note: Use browser_resize to change viewport. Take browser_snapshot after resize to check for overflow or clipping in text.

category.name: UI Consistency
category.tc: One TC per component type with multiple instances — compare HTML structure across all instances
Generated automatically from the component registry during test plan creation

standard.name: Snapshot Before Screenshot
standard.rule: ALWAYS call browser_snapshot to confirm expected state in text BEFORE calling browser_take_screenshot
If snapshot does not confirm expected state, mark FAIL with snapshot text — no screenshot needed

standard.name: One Screenshot Per Test Case
standard.minimum: Every PASS test case must have at least one AFTER screenshot
standard.recommended: BEFORE + AFTER pair for state-change tests (create, update, delete, toggle)
standard.skip: BEFORE screenshot not required for smoke tests and navigation tests

standard.name: Screenshot Must Match Assertion
standard.rule: If test asserts "user sees a success message", screenshot must show that success message
If test asserts "item is deleted from list", screenshot must show the list WITHOUT that item
If screenshot does not show the asserted state, the test is FAIL — not PASS

standard.name: Annotation Required for Specific Elements
standard.rule: If test verifies a specific button, form field, error message, list item, or UI element — annotate it
Full-page screenshots for page-load tests and navigation tests do not require annotation

standard.name: Annotation Gate — Hard Stop Before Screenshot
standard.rule: After calling browser_evaluate with any inject snippet, check the return value BEFORE calling browser_take_screenshot
Return value true → overlay is present and visible. Proceed to screenshot.

Return value false or null → the target element was not found or had zero bounding-box dimensions. FAIL the TC immediately with: "Annotation target not found — element not rendered or off-screen." Do NOT take the screenshot.
A screenshot with no visible red overlay is not valid evidence. It could show any state and proves nothing specific.
standard.why-this-matters: The previous pattern called inject then screenshot with no check in between. If the element was not in the DOM (e.g., the snapshot had stale coordinates, the element was inside a closed dropdown, or the page had scrolled), the screenshot would fire on a blank page with no annotation — and then pass silently unless the evaluator caught it. The gate makes the failure immediate and explicit instead of deferred.

standard.name: Proof Folder Separation
standard.rule: All TC pass-evidence screenshots (TC-NNN-after.png, TC-NNN-before.png) go into the PROOF_DIR subfolder, not the base SNAPSHOTS_DIR
Discovery screenshots (discovery-home.png) and temporary/debug shots stay in the base screenshots/ folder
PROOF_DIR is named proof-[TICKET_ID] when a ticket is set, or proof-[hostname]-[YYYY-MM-DD] otherwise
standard.why-this-matters: When the screenshots/ folder contains dozens of files, it is hard to find the actual pass-evidence images. The proof subfolder contains only the annotated, confirmed-pass screenshots — exactly what goes into a report or bug ticket.

cross-session-memory.description: Three persistent files per task workspace that survive across sessions. Load at start. Write during the session. Never delete entries.

file.name: ui-quirks.md
file.purpose: Records tricky UI elements — wrong-click corrections, unstable selectors, elements that behave differently from their ARIA role suggests.
file.write-when: Immediately after any navigation correction or unexpected element behavior.
file.example: | "Save" button | /settings | click parent div[data-action="save"], not the button | TC-007 |

file.name: known-failures.md
file.purpose: Records flows that were BLOCKED — the exact step that failed and what was tried. Prevents wasting time re-discovering the same blocker.
file.write-when: Immediately after marking any test case BLOCKED.
file.format: | Flow | Step | Blocking reason | Tried | Date |
file.example: | Checkout | Step 2: payment form | iframe not accessible via MCP | direct nav + evaluate | 2026-05-29 |
file.re-attempt-rule: If the same flow and step appear in known-failures.md: try ONE different approach. If that also fails: mark BLOCKED immediately, do not repeat the same approaches.

file.name: baselines/
file.purpose: Reference screenshots for pixelmatch comparison. One PNG per page visited.
file.write-when: First time a page is tested in a new session (no baseline exists).
file.naming: [page-slug].png where slug = URL path with / replaced by - (e.g. /products/list → products-list.png)
file.never: Never overwrite a baseline automatically. Only update when user explicitly approves.

temp-logging-protocol.purpose: Allow verification of backend operations that produce no visible UI confirmation

legitimate-use-cases.case: An async background job is triggered — no immediate success message appears in the UI
A webhook is sent to an external service — UI shows no confirmation
An audit log entry is created — the app has no UI that exposes the audit log

illegitimate-use-cases.case: The UI shows a success toast but checking logs is easier — use the UI
The UI shows a list that should update — navigate back to the list
You have not fully explored the UI for confirmation yet — keep exploring before resorting to logs

protocol.step: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="[operation] handler controller service" — find the function that handles the operation. If you need to trace callers or find which module wires this up, add mode="graph" to the same call.
Read the target file with the Read tool
Add: console.log('[E2E-TEMP] TC-NNN: [description]'); immediately after the operation completes
Perform the browser action that triggers the function
Call browser_console_messages — confirm the log line appears with the correct TC-NNN prefix
Edit the file to remove the log line
Read the file again to confirm the log line is gone — MANDATORY
In plan.md: PASS | verified via temp-log (removed)

temp-logging-protocol.warning: If used more than 2 times in one session: "WARNING: Temp-logging used N times. Each must genuinely lack a visible UI confirmation. Review each case."
temp-logging-protocol.absolute-rule: NEVER leave temp-log statements in the codebase after the test session ends. Verify removal in Step 7.

flow-map-generation.description: Required phase between discovery and test plan. Maps every multi-step user flow before any test cases are written. Tests come from flows — not from what's visible on one page.
flow-map-generation.why: The biggest cause of skipped test coverage is building test cases from page observation alone. A page shows what's on it right now — not what happens after you interact with it, not what state is required before you arrive, not how the flow branches on error. The flow map captures all of that before a single test case is written.

required-flows.flow: All authentication flows (login, logout, register, forgot password)
Every CRUD operation spanning more than one page
Every multi-step wizard or checkout process
Any flow that requires prior state (login-gated, cart-required, etc.)
Any flow that differs by user role

flow-map-generation.source-reference-rule: Every step in the flow map must name the triggering UI element. "click button 'Place Order'" not "proceed to next step". During test execution: if that element isn't in the DOM at that URL, the test is BLOCKED. Never silently skip a step because the element isn't found.
flow-map-generation.test-case-linkage: Every test case in plan.md references its parent flow. Format: TC-NNN [Flow: Checkout, Step 2] — description A test case without a flow reference is not a valid test case.

app-discovery-methodology.purpose: Understand an unfamiliar app before generating test cases. Two legal channels: RAG codebase search and browser navigation. No database access.

rag-discovery.query: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="routes pages navigation URL paths", limit=6, mode="graph"
POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="authentication login session user roles JWT cookie", limit=5, mode="graph"
POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", query="form submit create update delete entity model schema", limit=5, mode="graph"
rag-discovery.note: mode="graph" is used here because routes, auth, and entity modules have rich import/inheritance relationships — graph mode surfaces structural neighbours (middleware, base controllers, shared validators) alongside the semantic matches.
rag-discovery.extract: From results: route paths, entity names, auth mechanism, form structures, known features

browser-discovery.step: Navigate to root URL, take ONE screenshot for the landing page, then switch to browser_snapshot for all remaining discovery
From the snapshot, enumerate ALL nav links, buttons, and top-level interactive elements
Follow each top-level nav link, take browser_snapshot, record: page title, forms, lists, buttons, component types
Limit to 2 levels deep — this is reconnaissance, not exhaustive crawl

On each page, record for EVERY interactive element: HTML element type, ARIA role, visible label, and interaction model (click / keyboard / drag). This is the basis for the flow map steps and prevents wrong-click failures during test execution.
Note any elements that appear interactive but have unusual DOM structure (e.g. a div with onClick that looks like a button — record this as a potential quirk)

app-discovery-methodology.app-map-format:
## App Map — [URL]
**Date**: [date] **Scope**: [scope]
## Pages Discovered - / — [description] - /[page] — [description]
## Authentication - Required: yes/no - Login route: [path] - Protected routes: [list]
## Entities [entity names discovered]
## Key Flows [auth flows, CRUD flows, etc.]
## Component Registry | Component Type | Page | Selector Hint | N States / Size | |---|---|---|---| | [type] | [page] | [selector] | [count] |
## Startup Console Errors [any errors from initial load]

ui-scope-graph-strategy.overview: Before opening a browser, use ticket entities to build a "UI Pages in Scope" map. This tells you which pages THIS ticket actually touches — so you know where to focus testing and what gets mandatory coverage. Works the same way as the code exploration scope graph, adapted for UI routes instead of source files.
ui-scope-graph-strategy.when-to-run: When a ticket ID or ticket content is available at test start. If there is no ticket, skip this and proceed with general app discovery.
ui-scope-graph-strategy.step: Extract entities from the ticket. Sources in priority order: - analysis.md "Code Entities" section (file paths, PascalCase class/service names, endpoint paths, model/table names) - ticket.md raw text — look for route paths (/users, /admin), component names, feature names, model names - Fall back to key noun phrases from the ticket summary Cap at 10 most specific entities.

For each entity, run BOTH searches. Never skip either. Call 1 — vector: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", project_path=..., query="[entity]", mode="vector", limit=3 Call 2 — graph: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", project_path=..., query="[entity]", mode="graph", limit=3 Vector finds semantically similar files; graph finds structural neighbours via imports and inheritance.

From all results, identify files that render UI or define routes: - Route files (*Router*, *routes*, *Routes*, app.tsx, _app.tsx, pages/) - Page components (page, Page, View, Screen in name or path) - Controller actions with [HttpGet] / [Route] attributes Map each file to its URL path (from the route definition or page directory structure).

Write "## UI Pages in Scope (Graph Map)" to context.md: | URL/Route | File | Seed Entity | How Connected | |-----------|------|-------------|---------------| | /products | src/pages/Products.tsx | ProductService | graph neighbour | Update this map as you discover more pages during browser crawl.
ui-scope-graph-strategy.rule: NEVER run only vector or only graph. Both calls are mandatory. Graph traversal finds the route wiring and middleware that semantic search alone misses.
ui-scope-graph-strategy.mandatory-coverage: Every page in the UI Pages in Scope map gets mandatory test coverage: - At minimum: 1 navigation TC confirming the page loads - Plus 1 TC per form or interactive action on that page These cannot be omitted or marked BLOCKED for difficulty. Pages NOT in the scope map still get smoke test coverage — just not mandatory per-action coverage.
ui-scope-graph-strategy.fallback: If no ticket is available, or if the project is not indexed, skip this step. Use the general app-discovery-methodology queries instead. Note the gap in context.md.
